headline: PNP Tightens Service-Firearm Accountability After School Shooting Incidents
seoTitle: PNP Tightens Service Firearm Accountability | FMB News
seoDescription: The PNP ordered commanders nationwide to reinforce proper storage and handling of police-issued firearms following recent school shooting incidents involving government-linked weapons.
deck: Police commanders were told to reinforce secure firearm handling and prevent children or other unauthorized people from gaining access to service weapons.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: Philippine National Police chief Gen. Jose Melencio Nartatez Jr. ordered police commanders nationwide to reinforce accountability measures for police-issued firearms, particularly when officers are off duty and weapons are kept at home.

The publicly corroborated directive emphasizes that service firearms must be stored where children and other unauthorized persons cannot access them. The move follows recent school shooting incidents involving firearms linked to government personnel.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: The approved FMB News brief also described specific lockbox requirements, vehicle-storage prohibitions and administrative penalties. Those details were not independently reproduced in the current primary or reliably indexed reporting available during this publication run, so FMB News is not presenting them as confirmed policy terms.

Separately, Cebu provincial police reported that an unloaded .357 revolver was found in the bag of a 14-year-old Grade 9 student at Lut-od National High School in Pinamungajan on August 20. Police said the firearm allegedly belonged to the student's grandfather and had been taken from a cabinet at home.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: Recent incidents have focused attention on how firearms assigned to public personnel are secured outside duty hours. Stronger custody practices can reduce the risk of accidental access, theft and misuse by minors or other unauthorized people.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Watch for a formal PNP memorandum or Firearms and Explosives Office guidance spelling out any new inspection procedures, storage standards or sanctions beyond the accountability reminders already confirmed publicly.
